FIX ROUND 675b for story #675 (recipes add in a folder repository makes it a recipe library: every default silently leaves .brokkr/state for .forge), on branch story-675-recipes-add-folder, already checked out in this worktree at 1dc5f277.

You are fixing exactly the finding below and its class, nothing beside them. The story's own facts follow under HOST FACTS. Decision 0071 (the architectural principles) is ACCEPTED. Build to it.

HISTORY OF THE BRANCH
- 47eb47a3: #634 slice B's head (story-634-slice-b, landing in parallel as its own PR). This branch is STACKED on it because slice B rewrites the verb this story changes. Your diff is judged against 47eb47a3.
- 1dc5f277 (story run implement-story-675-recipes-add--a5f143ee): the story. recipes::add calls refuse_folder before it clones, copies or creates anything; refuse_folder walks places::Layout::discover from the workspace and from `standing(absolute(--dir))`, the nearest ancestor of --dir at which an entry stands, and refuses recipes::InFolder { root } when either walk finds Kind::Folder.
- Its review returned a SECURITY-HOLD (the adversarial seat's HIGH; the chief reproduced it on the HEAD binary). Correctness and the glm seat were clean.
- When you are done, the branch is the above plus ONE new commit of yours. Do not rebase, squash or amend.

FIX THIS, proved by binding tests and removal controls (plant the shape, see the test fail with the stated text, remove the plant):
1. HIGH (security; #675's acceptance "from any directory whose --dir resolves inside the folder repository, refuses by name and writes nothing"; decision 0083 ruling 1; 0071 ruling 10: what is judged must be what the effect writes). crates/brokkr-cli/src/recipes.rs refuse_folder/standing (~360-382). std::path::absolute keeps `..`, and standing() walks LEXICAL ancestors, so a `..` that follows an absent component is judged from the wrong place. Reproduction from the review: P=$(mktemp -d); git init P/folder; `brokkr init .` in P/folder; P/agents and P/adapters copied from P/folder/.brokkr so the copy compiles; from P, `brokkr recipes add P/folder/.brokkr --name x --dir missing/../folder/recipes` printed "added recipe 'x' (bdca92a7ae29) at missing/../folder/recipes/x" and exited 0. Afterwards P/missing and P/folder/recipes/x/bundle.json existed, and `brokkr runs` in P/folder read .forge/forge.db: the silent default switch #675 exists to refuse. With a source that fails to compile, the same command still created P/missing and P/folder/recipes/ before the compile removed the copy. The every-ancestor-absent walk stopped at P (Bare); create_dir_all then made `missing` and landed `../folder/recipes` inside the folder repository.
   THE CLASS: the place judged is not the place written. Sweep it across every path `add` writes:
   a. --dir: judge the destination as create_dir_all will make it. The smaller fail-closed form is preferred: refuse a --dir whose part after its nearest standing ancestor holds any component that is not a plain name (`..`, `.` beyond the first, a root or prefix), naming the --dir. Name in notes which form you took.
   b. --name: `dest = dir.join(name)` is written too. A --name that is not ONE plain path component (holds a separator, `..`, `.`, or is empty or absolute) can place the recipe outside --dir; with an existing <folder repo>/recipes/ directory, `--name ../../folder/recipes/x` from a sibling library lands a library mark in the folder repository. Refuse such a --name before anything is written, with its own exact text, as base_of (~244-262) already holds an `extends` base to a single plain component. Name the new refusal text in notes: the PR asks the operator to accept it.
   c. Anything else add creates before its refusal can fire (the clone's tempdir is outside the repository and is fine; name any other you find).
   Tests, each with exact text and a removal control recorded in the commit: in tests/recipes.rs, from outside the folder repository, `--dir missing/../<repo>/recipes` refuses with the InFolder text (or the new text, if form (a) refuses it first: say which), creates no <outside>/missing and no <repo>/recipes, and `brokkr runs` in the repository still reads .brokkr/state/forge.db; a --name with `..` from a sibling library, with <repo>/recipes/ already present as an empty directory, refuses and writes nothing under <repo>/recipes; a plain --name in a library or bare directory installs exactly as today (the existing tests keep their names and assertions). A unit test in recipes/tests.rs binds each refusal by type, not text (decision 0071 ruling 8).

CARRY, do not change (each goes in your notes for the PR, with the operator's reading):
- `--dir ""` now refuses as PlacesError::Unreadable where before it installed into the working directory (a degenerate input).
- standing()'s `unwrap_or(Ok(path))` fallback may be unreachable for an absolute path: if your change keeps it, the exact-coverage gate (the controller's) is the authority; delete code you make unreachable.
- The workspace layout is walked twice per add (setup::recipes, then refuse_folder): one judgement called twice. Leave it.

For the implement phase: fix, then run, all clean, from the worktree root: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy -p brokkr-cli --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings; cargo test -p brokkr-cli --lib recipes::; cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test it recipes:: brokkr_folder:: init_doctor:: suppressions::; typos --hidden; quality/ratchet.sh files, clones and api; git diff --check. No public API item moves. Do not run scripts/coverage-exact.sh; the controller runs it. Every new production line and branch is reachable by a test. A new test file is named *_tests.rs or tests.rs.

Every review position, panel member or chief, is READ-ONLY: it changes no tracked file and makes no commit, whatever this text asks. It reports each finding. Only the implement phase fixes a finding the review returns.

Commit one signed-off commit (git commit -s), message "cli: <what changed> (#675)" in the repository's style, ending with the line "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>". Never push. Run every command in the foreground and wait for it: never background a command or schedule a wake-up, because a headless seat ends when it waits.

Threat model (operator ruling, 2026-09-26): catch realistic accidental misuse, and fail closed on what cannot be read. The `..`-after-absent shape is unusual, but the fix is small and fail-closed; build it.

HOST FACTS AND PARALLEL WORK

- Main is origin/main as you find it (f73ee03a or later). Main lands only through the merge queue. Decision 0083 is ACCEPTED (docs/decisions/0083-an-adopters-brokkr-lives-in-one-folder.md): an adopter's Brokkr lives in one `.brokkr/` folder at the repository root. brokkr-runtime src/places.rs is the ONE judgement of a layout (`Layout::discover`, `Kind::{Folder, Library, Bare}`, `places::root`), and brokkr-cli src/folder.rs holds the CLI's words (`folder::Layout`, `FolderError`).
  - READ these whole before you start: issue #675 (below) and its comments; decision 0083's rulings 1 and 5; the operator's rulings on #634 (comments of 2026-10-13 and 2026-10-14).
- THIS BRANCH IS STACKED. story-675-recipes-add-folder is cut from story-634-slice-b at 47eb47a3, NOT from main, because #634 slice B (landing in parallel as its own PR) rewrites the verb this story changes: crates/brokkr-cli/src/verbs/setup.rs `recipes()` now discovers the layout and calls `layout.refuse_old()?` before `recipes::add`. Build on what you find. Your diff is judged against 47eb47a3; do not change any slice B line except where this story needs it, and name each such hunk in notes. The controller merges main into this branch after slice B lands.
- Operator ruling, 2026-09-26, the threat model for every gate: catch realistic ACCIDENTAL misuse, and fail closed on what cannot be read. A deliberate, exotic evasion is a LOW residual.
- Host tools as ci.yml pins them. typos, shellcheck and actionlint live in ~/.local/bin; jscpd, cargo-shear and cargo-crap in ~/.cargo/bin. Public-API snapshots (quality/public-api/<crate>.txt) come from cargo-public-api 0.52.0 on the pinned nightly, and quality/README.md says how to regenerate one. The complexity ratchet (cargo-crap 0.5.0) judges a MOVED function as new: CC 15 or under and 100 lines or under. An existing function may grow to 15 or to its baseline CC, whichever is higher.
- Test modules: the exact-coverage gate leaves out only files named tests.rs or *_tests.rs / *-tests.rs (scripts/coverage-exact.sh test_files). A test submodule named otherwise counts as PRODUCTION, and its panic arms read as uncovered lines. Name every new test file *_tests.rs.
- Tests that spawn processes: since #403 the test binary is a subreaper engine with one attempt registry. A test that drives a run through the CLI builds its engine through tests/support/engine.rs (#646), which gives it a private TMPDIR. brokkr-cli's integration tests are one binary (tests/it.rs), so one test file reaches another's helpers as `crate::<file>::<item>` once they are pub(crate). Slice B's tests plant a folder repository by `git init` then `brokkr init .` (tests/brokkr_folder.rs, tests/init_doctor.rs); reuse their helpers rather than copying them (the clones ratchet).
- The doc_truth and suppressions scanners read TRACKED files only: `git add -N` a new file before running them.
- OPERATOR RULING on #675, 2026-10-15: option A. `recipes add` refuses in a folder repository, names the folder, and writes nothing. In a recipe library or a bare repository it behaves exactly as today. The issue's acceptance stands.
- WHAT TO BUILD (the controller's reading of the ruling and the acceptance; name in notes any place you depart from it):
  1. `brokkr recipes add` refuses, before it clones, copies or creates any directory, when EITHER (a) the working directory's layout (the one setup::recipes already discovers) is `Kind::Folder`, OR (b) `--dir`, made absolute against the working directory, resolves inside a folder repository: discover the layout from `--dir`'s nearest existing ancestor (it may not exist yet; `recipes add` creates it), and refuse when that layout is `Kind::Folder`. (b) catches `--dir` pointing into a folder repository from outside it, and `--dir .brokkr/recipes` from inside. A discovery refusal on that walk (a nested `.brokkr`, an unreadable entry) refuses in its own words: fail closed.
  2. The refusal names the folder and says why, in one form for both cases, for example: "<root> keeps its Brokkr in <root>/.brokkr (decision 0083): recipes add would install a recipe library there, which outranks the folder and moves every default out of it (#675); a folder repository's bundle is .brokkr/ itself, and recipes add writes nothing here". Keep it short and exact; the PR names the final text for the operator.
  3. Keep the refusal OUT of `FolderError`: its Display is at the complexity ceiling (CC 15; slice B's 77ed3503 had to move init's refusals into folder/admit.rs's own `Refused` for this reason). Give it its own small typed error (decision 0071 ruling 8: callers and tests match the type, never the text) in recipes.rs or beside it.
  4. `recipes list` and `recipes show` are unchanged in every layout: they write nothing.
- TESTS (exact text, exact paths, each with a removal control recorded in notes and the commit):
  - a folder repository (git init + brokkr init .): `recipes add <local bundle> --name x` from the root refuses with the exact text; no `recipes/` is created; the tree under `.brokkr/` is byte-identical before and after; a following `brokkr runs` (or the layout's state path) still reads `.brokkr/state/forge.db`, not `.forge/`.
  - the same from a subdirectory of the folder repository (default `--dir` resolves to `<sub>/recipes`, inside the repository): refuses.
  - from a bare directory OUTSIDE the folder repository with `--dir <folder repo>/recipes`: refuses, and writes nothing there.
  - `--dir <folder repo>/.brokkr/recipes` from the root: refuses.
  - a recipe library (Brokkr's own layout, `recipes/*/bundle.json`) and a bare repository: `recipes add` installs exactly as today (existing tests in tests/recipes.rs and src/recipes/tests.rs keep their names and assertions).
  - an unreadable ancestor on the `--dir` walk refuses (fail closed), if you can make one on Linux without root; otherwise name it in notes.
- Other work runs in parallel. Stay out of these unless your story needs them, and name any hunk you make in them:
  - #634 slice B's landing (story-634-slice-b in another worktree): folder.rs, folder/*, init.rs, doctor/folder.rs, verbs/setup.rs, tests/init_doctor.rs, tests/brokkr_folder.rs, tests/init_stacks.rs, tests/boundary_verbs.rs. Change setup.rs's `recipes()` only as this story needs.
  - Decision 0065 slice two (the-forge-b9; NEVER message it, or any brokkr-wt-* seat). It owns brokkr-protocol broker*, hands*, native_controls*, secret*, adapters* and transcript.rs, and brokkr-cli's cli_args.rs, doctor.rs and the capability tests, among others. This story needs none of them.
- Gates as usual: cargo test -p brokkr-cli --lib recipes::, cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test it recipes:: brokkr_folder:: init_doctor:: suppressions::, clippy -D warnings, fmt, typos --hidden, quality/ratchet.sh files, clones and api. No public API item moves in any crate. If you change help text (the `--dir` doc comment, say), leave docs/reference/cli.md and say so: the controller regenerates it. The exact-coverage gate is the controller's.
- One more lane beside you: #349 slice 5 (brokkr-wt-349e): brokkr-runtime dialect.rs, bundle.rs, engine.rs, engine/sequence.rs. It touches no brokkr-cli file.

instructions.analyze:
# OpenSpec analyze

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.
instructions.clarify:
# OpenSpec clarify

Judge underspecified areas, unquantified language, missing decisions, capability/delta mismatches, and requirements without adequate scenarios. Return every ambiguity with the evidence needed to settle it; zero findings is clear.
instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.
instructions.implement:
# OpenSpec tasks

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/tasks.md` as numbered groups of checkboxes. Name the requirement served by every task. On return, repair the breakdown and its requirement coverage before implementation resumes.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `recipes/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.
